scenes.card: Odysseus's old dog, neglected for twenty years, recognizes his master's voice, wags his tail, and dies.

subs.text: Scene three.
Argos Recognizes His Master.
Near the palace Odysseus sees his old dog Argos lying neglected on dung.
The old hound knows him.
He lifts his head out of the dung, drops his ears, and beats his tail,
but he has no strength left to rise and come.
Eumaeus, that dog on the heap.
There is a fine shape under all that dirt.
Was he a hunter once, or only a table dog kept for show?
Twenty years he waited, and one look was enough.
The dark of death takes Argos in the moment he has seen his master again.

subs.text: Scene five.
Antinous Throws the Stool.
I had a house and men of my own once, and I gave to any beggar who came.
Then Egypt swallowed it.
My crew were cut down along the river and I was sold from hand to hand until I came to this door.
What god dumped this plague on our dinner?
Back from the table, you shameless thing, before you find an Egypt worse than the first.
Your body is handsome, but there is no mind inside it.
Sitting in another man's house you would not give a grain of salt from a table that is not yours.
Antinous hurls a footstool into his shoulder.
Hear me, gods, and you avengers of the poor, if a beggar has any claim on heaven.
Let Antinous meet his death before his wedding day.
Even the other suitors condemn the violation of a stranger.

Penelope Summons the Stranger.
Do not mistake my silence.
Eumaeus to bring him for questioning?

There are hard hands in that hall, and one has already found me.
Let me come to her at dusk when the light is gone.
The stranger is no fool.
He sees these men for exactly what they are.
Let him come when the hall empties, and he will sit by my fire and say whatever he likes.
Telemachus sneezes loudly.
Did you hear that?
My words are sealed.
Every one of these men will meet his death.

scenes.world: An upper chamber of a stone palace and the dim feasting hall below, late afternoon light through narrow windows.

captain.asks: Hold on Penelope as she laughs at the sneeze, so a figure forms in the upper room out of sound.
diagnosis: The veiled figure against a patterned wall with window light is a real find and anchors the room.
Penelope's laugh is a crop of a mouth and chin; there is no held face to hold.
Hats, a telephone and restaurant tables keep pulling the palace into the 1930s.

sign.operation: Static wide of the night hall.

scenes.world: A dim feasting hall at night, embers and smoky lamplight, tables strewn with remains, men lounging.

captain.asks: Hold one static wide of the night hall so bodies lounging in attitude carry the exhausted feast.
diagnosis: There is no hall: a carousel, a pram on a poster street and a cafe window stand in for it.
The static wide the sign asks for does not exist; the scene is darkness and two found faces.
The beggar's recurring eyes are the only thread a stranger can hold.

prologue: The disguised king walks into his own palace for the first time in twenty years. He must endure insults from the suitors without giving himself away.
